request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A rate can now have a to-date, and all four tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration `V27__rate_to.sql` adds a `to_date` column to rates.
- **Server:**
  - The rate form accepts a to-date. A to-date that isn't a valid date, or is before the from-date, is refused, and a refused rate writes nothing.
  - `RATE_SET` gets ` to=<date>` at the end of the line when a to-date was given.
  - Setting a rate again for the same grade and from-date also replaces its to-date. Leaving the to-date blank clears it.
  - `Rate.on` (`rate/Rate.java`) still picks the rate with the latest from-date on or before the claim's date, but now returns no rate if that rate's to-date has passed. The claim's due, the totals, statements and the late charge all get their rate from it, so they follow without further changes.
- **Front end:** the form has a `rate-form-to` field, each rate row shows `rate-to`, and `rateOf` uses the same rule as the server.

**A change to how the person's total works.** Before, a person's due-total showed n/a whenever their grade had no rate on the sheet's today, unless a claim kept its own figure. Under that rule the first test failed: once a rate had ended, the total went to n/a even though older claims still had a due. A claim now also counts as having its own figure if it is dated on or before today and a rate gave it a due on its date. I made this change in `Person.figureApartFrom` on the server and in `personDueCents` on the front end.

This doesn't change any result for sheets without to-dates. There, a grade with no rate today never had a rate on an earlier date either, so the new condition can't apply.
